# Build learning platform UI shell

> You are a senior Frontend Engineer and UI/UX developer.
>
> Your task is to build ONLY the frontend shell for a Learning Platform similar to Programiz Pro.
>
> Do NOT implement any backend logic.
> Do NOT implement authentication.
> Do NOT implement routing.
> Do NOT implement JSON loading.
> Do NOT implement the compiler.
> Do NOT hardcode course data except for placeholder content.
>
> The objective is to create a reusable UI shell that can later render dynamic lessons.
>
> The layout must occupy the entire viewport.
>
> -------------------------------------------------
>
> The page contains three primary sections.
>
> LEFT SIDEBAR
> - Fixed width
> - Scrollable independently
> - Displays Course Title
> - Displays Modules
> - Each module expands into lessons
> - Active lesson should be highlighted
> - Completed lessons should display a check icon
> - Locked lessons should appear disabled
> - Collapse/Expand animation
>
> CENTER CONTENT PANEL
> - Scrollable independently
> - Displays Lesson Title
> - Displays lesson blocks
> - Use placeholder content
> - Create placeholder blocks for:
>     Heading
>     Paragraph
>     Code Block
>     Image Placeholder
>     Quiz Placeholder
>     Exercise Placeholder
>     AI Explanation Placeholder
> - Maintain generous spacing
> - Maximum readable width
> - Responsive typography
>
> RIGHT PANEL
> - Fixed width
> - Placeholder compiler
> - Header containing:
>     Language
>     Run Button
>     Reset Button
> - Editor placeholder
> - Output placeholder
> - Error placeholder
>
> -------------------------------------------------
>
> Top Navigation
>
> Include a sticky top navigation bar containing
>
> - Course Name
> - Current Lesson
> - Previous Lesson Button
> - Next Lesson Button
> - Progress Indicator
>
> -------------------------------------------------
>
> Responsive Behaviour
>
> Desktop:
> Three-column layout
>
> Tablet:
> Sidebar collapses
>
> Mobile:
> Sidebar becomes drawer
> Compiler moves below lesson
>
> -------------------------------------------------
>
> Design
>
> Modern
> Minimal
> Professional
>
> Do not use bright colors.
>
> Rounded corners
>
> Subtle shadows
>
> Proper spacing
>
> Smooth transitions
>
> The layout should feel like a premium coding education platform.
>
> -------------------------------------------------
>
> The code should be modular and component-based.
>
> Create reusable components for every major section.
>
> No business logic.
> Only UI.

Implemented a generic, extensible `BlockRenderer`.

Architecture:

- [BlockRenderer.jsx](./src/components/BlockRenderer.jsx) only iterates over blocks and delegates rendering.
- [blockRegistry.js](./src/components/blockRegistry.js) owns the type-to-component mapping.
- No `if/else` or `switch` chains.
- Unknown types render [UnknownBlock.jsx](./src/components/blocks/UnknownBlock.jsx).

## Root causes

1. The wrong course was selected.

[course-metadata.json](./public/courses/course-metadata.json:2) used `course-placeholder` as `defaultCourseId`. Because `App` supplies no explicit course ID, [courseRepository.js](./src/course/courseRepository.js:18) selected `/courses/learning-platform.json`.

That placeholder contains:

- 8 lessons
- Only 7 blocks total
- 7 lessons with empty `blocks` arrays

The Python course was never loaded.

2. The Course Loader lacked model normalization.

`python-course.json` follows the canonical Learning Engine schema, while the existing UI expects additional view-model properties such as:

- `name`
- `shortMark`
- `categoryLabel`
- Flattened navigation labels
- `ui`
- `sidebar`
- `compiler`
- `module.initiallyOpen`
- `module.meta`
- `lesson.numberLabel`
- `lesson.details`

The loader previously passed raw JSON directly to the UI. Switching the default course alone would therefore have exposed missing shell properties.

## Pipeline verification

After the repair:

| Stage | Verified result |
|---|---|
| Metadata selection | `mi-tutora-python-course` |
| Course source | `/courses/python-course.json` |
| Schema validation | Valid |
| Course model | `MI Tutora Python Course` |
| Modules | 6 |
| Lessons | 68 |
| Total blocks | 406 |
| Empty Python lessons | 0 |
| Default module | `module-1-getting-started-with-python` |
| Default lesson | `lesson-1-1-introduction-to-python` |
| Default lesson blocks | 12 |
| `currentBlockList` | 12 |
| Renderer property | `blocks` |
| Duplicate lesson IDs | None |
| Invalid navigation targets | None |
| Unknown block types | None |

The JSON and renderer both use `lesson.blocks`; there is no property-name mismatch.

## Fixes applied

- Changed the default course to `mi-tutora-python-course` in [course-metadata.json](./public/courses/course-metadata.json:2).
- Added [createCourseModel.js](./src/course/createCourseModel.js) to map canonical course JSON into the existing UI model without modifying modules, lessons, IDs, navigation, or blocks.
- Updated [CourseLoader.jsx](./src/course/CourseLoader.jsx:33) to normalize the loaded course before creating navigation state.

The empty state was displayed silently because both [courseNavigation.js](./src/course/courseNavigation.js:102) and [BlockRenderer.jsx](./src/components/BlockRenderer.jsx:12) intentionally fall back to an empty array when blocks are absent. With the placeholder course selected, this fallback behaved as designed and concealed the incorrect course selection.

> Investigate why Vite is attempting to optimize a dependency named python, resulting in python-*.js being generated under node_modules/.vite/deps. Search the entire project and dependency graph for imports or packages named python, determine the exact source, and fix the root cause rather than masking it. Do not change runtime behavior or compiler logic.

<details><summary>3 previous messages</summary>

> I’ll trace this from Vite’s optimizer metadata back through the exact import chain, including Monaco’s Python registration module and the lockfile. I’ll only change the dependency boundary responsible for the misleading optimized dependency name, not editor or runtime behavior.
>
> The dependency graph has no npm package named `python`. The exact source is Monaco’s Python registration module: our editor imports `monaco-editor/languages/definitions/python/register`, and that module declares `loader: () => import('./python.js')`. Vite treats that lazy language payload as its own dependency/chunk named `python`. I’m replacing that registration wrapper with direct Python language configuration inside the already-lazy Monaco component.
>
> <details><summary>Edited a file</summary>
>
> - Wrote `./src/components/MonacoCodeEditor.jsx` (+14 -1)
>
> </details>
</details>

Root cause identified and fixed.

The project does not contain or depend on an npm package named `python`; `npm ls python --all` returns an empty dependency tree.

The artifact came from this Monaco import:

```js
import 'monaco-editor/languages/definitions/python/register';
```

Monaco’s registration module internally contains:

```js
loader: () => import('./python.js')
```

Vite interpreted that dynamic language payload as a separate dependency/chunk and named it `python-*.js`.

The fix replaces Monaco’s dynamic registration wrapper with direct imports of the same tokenizer and language configuration:

```js
import {
  conf as pythonConfiguration,
  language as pythonLanguage,
} from 'monaco-editor/languages/definitions/python/python';
```

These are registered directly through Monaco’s language APIs inside the existing lazy editor component. Python highlighting, indentation, brackets, comments, and editor behavior remain unchanged.

- Production build passed.

> Implement Sprint 8.2: Firestore Repository Foundation.
>
> This sprint builds the Firestore data layer only.
>
> Do NOT migrate any existing services or application features.
>
> ====================================================
> Objectives
> ====================================================
>
> Create a reusable Firestore repository architecture that will eventually replace localStorage repositories.
>
> No UI should change.
>
> No existing feature should change behavior.
>
> ====================================================
> Folder Structure
> ====================================================
>
> Create:
>
> src/
>     repositories/
>         firestore/
>
>             BaseRepository.js
>
>             UserRepository.js
>             CourseRepository.js
>             ProgressRepository.js
>             SettingsRepository.js
>             BookmarkRepository.js
>
>             paths.js
>             converters.js
>
> ====================================================
> BaseRepository
> ====================================================
>
> Implement reusable Firestore helpers.
>
> Support:
>
> - get(id)
> - set(id, data)
> - update(id, partial)
> - remove(id)
> - exists(id)
> - list()
> - query()
>
> Do not expose Firestore SDK details outside this class.
>
> ====================================================
> paths.js
> ====================================================
>
> Centralize every Firestore collection path.
>
> Provide helper functions for:
>
> users/{uid}
>
> users/{uid}/settings/preferences
>
> users/{uid}/progress/{courseId}
>
> users/{uid}/bookmarks
>
> users/{uid}/achievements
>
> users/{uid}/certificates
>
> users/{uid}/statistics/overview
>
> users/{uid}/coinTransactions
>
> courses/{courseId}
>
> practiceQuestions/{questionId}
>
> dailyChallenges/{challengeId}
>
> No collection names should be hardcoded elsewhere.
>
> ====================================================
> converters.js
> ====================================================
>
> Create reusable Firestore converters.
>
> Prepare converters for:
>
> - User
> - Course
> - Progress
> - Settings
> - Bookmark
>
> They may initially perform identity mapping, but all repositories should use them.
>
> ====================================================
> Repositories
> ====================================================
>
> Implement repositories for:
>
> UserRepository
>
> CourseRepository
>
> ProgressRepository
>
> SettingsRepository
>
> BookmarkRepository
>
> Each repository should extend BaseRepository where appropriate.
>
> Keep repository responsibilities limited to Firestore access only.
>
> No business logic.
>
> ====================================================
> Architecture Rules
> ====================================================
>
> - Components must not import Firebase.
> - Services must not import Firebase.
> - Firebase SDK imports remain isolated to src/firebase and src/repositories/firestore.
> - Existing localStorage services remain unchanged.
> - Existing repositories remain untouched.
>
> ====================================================
> Documentation

>
> Update:
>
> docs/architecture/firebase.md
>
> Add a section describing:
>
> - Repository layer
> - Firestore path conventions
> - Repository responsibilities
> - Why Firebase is isolated from the rest of the application
>
> ====================================================
> Validation
> ====================================================
>
> Verify:
>
> - Production build passes.
> - No UI changes.

Instrumented only the Firestore user-creation path.

Findings:

- Google `UserCredential` completes successfully.
- Firestore synchronization begins separately inside the auth-state observer.
- The first Firestore request is [AuthRepository.js](./src/auth/AuthRepository.js:91):
  ```js
  await this.users.exists(firebaseUser.uid)
  ```
- If that succeeds for a missing user, creation is awaited at [AuthRepository.js](./src/auth/AuthRepository.js:110).
- The underlying `setDoc()` is awaited at [BaseRepository.js](./src/repositories/firestore/BaseRepository.js:67).
- `AuthContext` receives the user only after synchronization finishes at [AuthService.js](./src/auth/AuthService.js:115).

The confirmed completion bug was the error path: Firestore failures were caught in `AuthService`, passed to a silent provider callback, and the authenticated user was never published. Navigation was not waiting on an unresolved promise—`AuthContext.user` remained `null` after the rejected Firestore operation.

- Credential receipt
- Firestore document path and existence check

- If it reaches `Awaiting setDoc`, failure is [BaseRepository.js](./src/repositories/firestore/BaseRepository.js:67).
- If `setDoc completed` appears, the failure is the read-back at line 69.

Persistence behavior:

- Reads check Firestore first for cross-device synchronization.
- Successful reads populate an in-memory user cache.
- Cached values are returned during temporary Firestore outages.
- Writes are serialized and update cache only after Firestore confirms success.
- Bookmark and certificate collection replacements use atomic batches.
- Firebase errors are converted to friendly `UserDataError` instances.
- Logout and account switching clear repositories, queued-write references, and cached data.
- Login hydrates Settings and reloads other data from Firestore as requested.

Audit complete. The current Firebase files are not being corrupted in the inspected loading pipeline.

### Findings

- Firebase uses `getBytes()` in [StorageContentLoader.js](./src/content/storage/StorageContentLoader.js:132).
- In the installed Firebase SDK, `getBytes()` returns an `ArrayBuffer`, not a `Uint8Array`. It is now converted into a complete zero-offset `Uint8Array` at line 139.
- UTF-8 decoding now explicitly uses:
  ```js
  new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(byteArray)
  ```
- `JSON.parse()` occurs exactly once, at [StorageContentLoader.js](./src/content/storage/StorageContentLoader.js:162).
- No `substring()`, `slice()`, `trim()`, `replace()`, stream decoding, or `String.fromCharCode()` modifies the content.
- [BaseContentService.js](./src/content/services/BaseContentService.js:31) and [CourseService.js](./src/content/services/CourseService.js:31) only pass parsed objects. Neither decodes, transforms, nor reparses JSON.

### Remote verification

All current Firebase course files downloaded and parsed successfully using the same Firebase Web SDK pipeline:

- `course.json`: 1,044 bytes
- `module-1.json`: 13,813 bytes
- `module-2.json`: 32,814 bytes
- `module-3.json`: 11,681 bytes
- `module-4.json`: 39,353 bytes
- `module-5.json`: 31,068 bytes
- `module-6.json`: 17,583 bytes

Each downloaded byte length matched its Firebase Storage metadata size.

Therefore, there is no underlying Firebase error in the reproduced request. `getBytes()` succeeds; the reported error originates at `JSON.parse()`, not Firebase Storage. With the currently uploaded files, that failure is not reproducible. This points to a stale deployed bundle/cache, different Firebase environment, or an earlier version of an uploaded object.

### Diagnostics added

Development logging now reports:

- Downloaded byte length
- Remote Storage object size
- Whether both sizes match
- Decoded string length
- First and last 100 characters
- Whether the raw decoded string ends in `}`
- Exact parser character index
- The surrounding 200 characters
- Original error, message, and stack

Firebase download errors are also retained as the original `cause` and logged instead of being swallowed.

One detail: the valid remote JSON files end with `}\n`, so the raw `endsWithClosingBrace` diagnostic is `false`. That is expected because the loader intentionally does not trim content.

- Only [StorageContentLoader.js](./src/content/storage/StorageContentLoader.js) was changed for this audit.

Compare it against Firebase Web SDK recommendations (getBlob(), getDownloadURL(), getStream() where applicable). If getBytes() is causing browser CORS/XHR issues, migrate the loader to the recommended browser API without changing the surrounding architecture.

<details><summary>3 previous messages</summary>

If the browser API is the issue, I’ll change only the download primitive inside `StorageContentLoader` and preserve its cache, validation, error, and service contracts.
>
> <details><summary>Searched the web</summary>
>
> Searched the web for `site:firebase.google.com/docs/storage/web/download-files getBlob getBytes getDownloadURL CORS ...`
>
> </details>
>
> The official guidance does not identify `getBytes()` as a Node-only or deprecated choice: it is a supported direct-download Web API and returns an `ArrayBuffer`. Both `getBytes()` and browser-only `getBlob()` require bucket CORS, while `getStream()` is Node-only. I’m checking the installed SDK implementation and current loader conversion before deciding whether any migration is justified.
</details>

`getBytes()` is appropriate for this browser application and should not be migrated.

Firebase officially supports three direct-download methods:

- `getBytes()` — browser-supported, returns an `ArrayBuffer`.
- `getBlob()` — browser-only, returns a `Blob`.
- `getStream()` — Node.js only.
- `getDownloadURL()` — returns a URL; retrieving JSON from that URL still requires an additional browser request.

Both `getBytes()` and `getBlob()` require the application origin to be allowed by the bucket’s CORS configuration. Switching between them would not resolve a CORS failure. Likewise, using `getDownloadURL()` followed by `fetch()` remains subject to browser CORS. [Firebase Web download guide](https://firebase.google.com/docs/storage/web/download-files), [Firebase Storage API reference](https://firebase.google.com/docs/reference/js/storage)

The current loader correctly:

1. Creates a Firebase Storage reference.
2. Calls `getBytes()`.
3. Receives the complete `ArrayBuffer`.
4. Creates a full `Uint8Array` view.
5. Decodes it using `TextDecoder('utf-8')`.
6. Parses the decoded text once.

For small JSON course modules, `getBytes()` is simpler than `getBlob()` and avoids an unnecessary Blob-to-text/ArrayBuffer conversion. `getStream()` cannot be used in the Vite browser application.

The previous live diagnostics also confirmed that the downloaded byte lengths matched Firebase object metadata and the bucket returned the necessary cross-origin headers. Therefore, `getBytes()` is not the source of the observed JSON parsing issue.

No implementation changes were made during this audit. Production build and `git diff --check` pass.

Implemented progress-write deduplication.

Root cause:

- Every persistence attempt generated fresh `updatedAt` and `lastOpened` values.
- No semantic comparison existed before calling Firestore.
- Newly created but equivalent progress objects therefore caused repeated writes.

Persistence paths audited:

- Current lesson changes
- Lesson visits and completion
- Quiz scores
- Exercise verification and completion
- Lesson bookmarks
- Course resets and development progress actions

All paths converge through:

```text
LearningProgressContext
→ progressRepository.save()
→ UserDataService.saveProgress()
→ ProgressRepository.set()
```

The fix was applied at this shared persistence boundary.

Changes in [UserDataService.js](./src/user-data/UserDataService.js):

- Added deterministic deep serialization with sorted object keys.
- Added immutable serialized snapshots of successfully loaded or persisted progress.
- Excluded `id`, `startedAt`, `lastOpened`, and `updatedAt` from semantic comparison.
- Compares inside the existing per-document write queue, preventing concurrent duplicate writes.
- Updates the snapshot only after Firestore succeeds.
- Clears snapshots on logout, progress deletion, and full progress reset.
- Retains cached data and retries after failed writes.

Validation results:

- Initial concurrent saves: exactly 1 write.
- Unchanged navigation state: 0 writes.
- Lesson completion: exactly 1 write.
- Production build passes.
- `git diff --check` passes.

Only `src/user-data/UserDataService.js` was modified for this fix.

>    - JSON schema

>
> Cache policy:
>
> - Always retain:
>   - previous module
>   - current module
>   - next module
>
> - Prefetch:
>   - next module only
>
> - If cache exceeds the configured window,
>   evict the farthest module.
>
> - Never issue duplicate downloads.
> - Never evict a module currently being viewed.
> - Navigation to an already cached module must be instant.
> - Background prefetch must never block rendering.
>
> Expose a configurable cache window (default 3 modules).
>
> Maintain compatibility with future:
> - lesson-level lazy loading
> - offline downloads
> - LRU extension
>

> # Sprint P1 – Exam Engine Foundation
>
> We are building the foundation for MiTutora's certification system.
>
> This sprint is NOT about AI proctoring yet.
>
> The objective is to build a reusable, production-quality Exam Engine that later supports AI proctoring, certification, integrity scoring, and future detectors.
>
> The implementation should follow the same engineering quality, architecture, and maintainability standards as the Learning Engine.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Architecture
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create the following structure:
>
> src/
> └── exam/
>     ├── components/
>     │   ├── EnvironmentCheck/
>     │   ├── BrowserCheck/
>     │   ├── WarningDialog/
>     │   └── DeveloperSimulator/
>     │
>     ├── context/
>     │   └── ExamProvider.jsx
>     │
>     ├── hooks/
>     │   └── useExam.js
>     │
>     ├── engine/
>     │   ├── ExamSession.js
>     │   ├── EventBus.js
>     │   ├── IntegrityEngine.js
>     │   ├── WarningManager.js
>     │   └── ExamConfig.js
>     │
>     ├── detectors/
>     │   └── BrowserMonitor.js
>     │
>     ├── models/
>     │   ├── ExamEvent.js
>     │   ├── IntegrityReport.js
>     │   └── EnvironmentResult.js
>     │
>     ├── pages/
>     │   ├── EnvironmentCheckPage.jsx
>     │   ├── ExamPage.jsx
>     │   └── ExamResultPage.jsx
>     │
>     └── data/
>         └── sampleExam.json
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Architecture Rules
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> This system must be event-driven.
>
> Every detector only emits events.
>
> Detectors MUST NOT:
>
> - calculate integrity score
> - show warnings
> - modify UI
> - know about reports
>
> The architecture must always be:
>
> Detector
>
> ↓
>
> EventBus
>
> ↓
>
> IntegrityEngine
>
> ↓
>
> WarningManager
>
> ↓
>
> Exam Report
>
> This separation is mandatory.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Exam Session
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create a reusable ExamSession.
>
> Responsibilities:
>
> - examId
> - candidateId
> - startTime
> - endTime
> - duration
> - current state
>
> Supported states:
>
> IDLE
>
> ↓
>
> ENVIRONMENT_CHECK
>
> ↓
>
> READY
>
> ↓
>
> RUNNING
>
> ↓
>
> COMPLETED
>
> Transitions should be explicit and validated.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Event Model
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create a reusable ExamEvent model.
>
> Each event should contain:
>
> {
>     id,
>     type,
>     timestamp,
>     durationMs,
>     severity,
>     metadata
> }
>
> Supported event types:
>
> TAB_SWITCH
>
> WINDOW_BLUR
>
> FULLSCREEN_EXIT
>
> COPY
>
> PASTE
>
> RIGHT_CLICK
>
> DEVTOOLS_OPEN
>
> WARNING
>
> CUSTOM
>
> Additional event types will be added later.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> EventBus
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Implement a lightweight publish/subscribe system.
>
> Required methods:
>
> emit()
>
> subscribe()
>
> unsubscribe()
>
> clear()
>
> Prevent duplicate listeners.
>
> No external libraries.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Integrity Engine
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create a reusable IntegrityEngine.
>
> Maintain:
>
> - integrity score
> - warning count
> - event timeline
>
> Initial score:
>
> 100
>
> Rules must NOT be hardcoded.
>
> Everything should come from ExamConfig.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> ExamConfig
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create a centralized configuration object.
>
> Example:
>
> {
>     browser: {
>         fullscreenRequired: true,
>         allowCopyPaste: false,
>         allowRightClick: false
>     },
>
>     integrity: {
>         initialScore: 100,
>         maxWarnings: 3
>     }
> }
>
> Future rules should be easy to add.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Warning Manager
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create a centralized WarningManager.
>
> Responsibilities:
>
> - queue warnings
> - avoid duplicate warnings
> - expose active warning
> - count warnings
>
> Do NOT implement UI here.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Browser Monitor
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Implement browser monitoring only.
>
> Detect:
>
> - visibilitychange
> - blur
> - focus
> - fullscreen exit
> - copy
> - paste
> - context menu
>
> Each detection must emit an ExamEvent.
>
> No scoring.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Environment Check
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create the first Environment Check page.
>
> This sprint only verifies:
>
> ✔ Browser compatibility
>
> ✔ Fullscreen support
>
> ✔ Window focus
>
> ✔ Required browser APIs
>
> Show a readiness screen.
>
> Camera and microphone will be implemented later.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Dummy Exam
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create a sample certification exam.
>
> 10 simple MCQs stored in JSON.
>
> Purpose:
>
> Validate:
>
> - navigation
> - timer
> - answer storage
> - submission
> - result generation
>
> No Firebase.
>
> No backend.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Exam Result
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Display:
>
> - Score
> - Integrity Score
> - Warning Count
> - Event Timeline
>
> Timeline must display every emitted event chronologically.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Developer Simulator
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> IMPORTANT
>
> Create a simulator available ONLY in development.
>
> Use:
>
> import.meta.env.DEV
>
> The simulator must NEVER appear in production builds.
>
> Buttons:
>
> - Tab Switch
> - Fullscreen Exit
> - Window Blur
> - Copy
> - Paste
> - Right Click
> - Warning
> - Reset
>
> Each button must emit an event through EventBus.
>
> Do NOT bypass the event system.
>
> The simulator should use the exact same pipeline that future AI detectors will use.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> General Requirements
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> - Follow existing MiTutora architecture.
> - Use React Context where appropriate.
> - No duplicated business logic.
> - No unnecessary re-renders.
> - No inline business logic inside UI components.
> - No console logging.
> - No TODO placeholders.
> - Production-ready code only.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Validation
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Verify:
>
> ✓ EventBus publishes/subscribes correctly.
>
> ✓ BrowserMonitor emits events.
>
> ✓ IntegrityEngine updates correctly.
>
> ✓ WarningManager tracks warnings.
>
> ✓ Timeline updates correctly.
>
> ✓ Simulator appears only in development.
>
> ✓ Production build passes.
>
> ✓ git diff --check passes.
>
> Do NOT implement camera, microphone, MediaPipe, TensorFlow, audio detection, phone detection, or AI proctoring in this sprint. Build only the reusable exam framework that all future detectors will plug into.

> # Sprint P3 – Continuous Integrity Monitoring
>
> Sprint P1 (Exam Engine), Sprint P2 (Vision & Environment Verification), and Sprint P2.5 (Verification UX & Hardening) are complete.
>
> This sprint introduces continuous integrity monitoring during an active exam.
>
> The objective is NOT to add new AI models.
>
> The objective is to convert the existing verification detectors into a continuous monitoring system that operates throughout the exam and produces evidence-driven integrity events.
>
> Do NOT implement:
>
> - Phone detection
> - Head pose estimation
> - Looking away detection
> - Eye tracking
> - Audio analysis
> - Object detection
> - Screen recording
>
> Those belong to future sprints.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Objectives
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Build a reusable integrity monitoring framework.
>
> The framework should continuously monitor the candidate throughout the exam.
>
> Every detector should publish events.
>
> Nothing should directly modify integrity scores except the Integrity Engine.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Architecture
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create the following additions.
>
> src/
> └── exam/
>     ├── engine/
>     │     DetectorManager.js
>     │     EventLifecycleManager.js
>     │
>     ├── monitoring/
>     │     MonitoringSession.js
>     │     MonitoringTimeline.js
>     │
>     ├── models/
>     │     IntegrityEvent.js
>     │     ActiveViolation.js
>     │
>     ├── components/
>     │     IntegrityPanel/
>     │     TimelinePanel/
>     │     ActiveViolations/
>     │
>     └── hooks/
>           useIntegrityMonitor.js
>
> Follow the existing architecture.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Detector Manager
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create a centralized DetectorManager.
>
> Responsibilities:
>
> - register detectors
> - unregister detectors
> - start detectors
> - stop detectors
> - pause detectors
> - resume detectors
> - destroy detectors
>
> Every detector should implement:
>
> start()
>
> stop()
>
> pause()
>
> resume()
>
> reset()
>
> destroy()
>
> getStatus()
>
> Future detectors must work without changing DetectorManager.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Continuous Monitoring
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> After the environment verification succeeds and the exam starts:
>
> Monitoring begins automatically.
>
> Monitoring ends only when:
>
> - the exam is submitted
> - the timer expires
> - the exam is cancelled
>
> No detector should stop while the exam is active.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Integrity Events
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Replace one-shot events with lifecycle events.
>
> Every violation should have:
>
> id
>
> type
>
> startedAt
>
> endedAt
>
> duration
>
> status
>
> metadata
>
> Status values:
>
> ACTIVE
>
> RECOVERED
>
> DISMISSED
>
> Example:
>
> Face Lost
>
> ↓
>
> ACTIVE
>
> ↓
>
> RECOVERED
>
> The same event should be updated instead of creating multiple duplicate events.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Event Lifecycle Manager
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create an EventLifecycleManager.
>
> Responsibilities:
>
> - create events
> - update events
> - recover events
> - close events
> - prevent duplicate active events
>
> If Face Lost is already active, do not create another Face Lost event.
>
> Instead update its duration.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Duration Tracking
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Every detector should report:
>
> Violation Started
>
> ↓
>
> Duration
>
> ↓
>
> Recovered
>
> Do NOT continuously emit duplicate events.
>
> The duration should update while the violation remains active.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Monitoring Timeline
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create a live chronological timeline.
>
> Example:
>
> 11:04:13
>
> Face Lost
>
> Started
>
> 11:04:19
>
> Recovered
>
> Duration
>
> 6 sec
>
> 11:12:02
>
> Fullscreen Exit
>
> Started
>
> 11:12:05
>
> Recovered
>
> Duration
>
> 3 sec
>
> The timeline should update in real time.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Integrity Engine
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> The Integrity Engine now listens continuously.
>
> Only the Integrity Engine may:
>
> - deduct integrity score
> - apply penalties
> - issue warnings
>
> Penalty values must remain configurable.
>
> Nothing should be hardcoded.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Warning Escalation
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Implement warning escalation.
>
> Example:
>
> Reminder
>
> ↓
>
> Warning
>
> ↓
>
> Final Warning
>
> ↓
>
> Violation Recorded
>
> Escalation thresholds must be configurable.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Recovery Handling
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> When a detector reports recovery:
>
> Face returns
>
> ↓
>
> Recover event
>
> Fullscreen restored
>
> ↓
>
> Recover event
>
> Browser focus returns
>
> ↓
>
> Recover event
>
> Recovery should update the existing event.
>
> Never create a second event.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Live Integrity Panel
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Create a live monitoring panel.
>
> Display:
>
> Integrity Score
>
> Current Warnings
>
> Active Violations
>
> Monitoring Status
>
> Current Detector Status
>
> Current Monitoring Time
>
> Timeline
>
> This panel should be available in development.
>
> It may optionally be shown in production for administrators later.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Development Monitor
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Development only.
>
> Visible only when:
>
> import.meta.env.DEV
>
> Extend the simulator.
>
> Allow:
>
> Start Face Lost
>
> Recover Face
>
> Start Fullscreen Exit
>
> Recover Fullscreen
>
> Start Browser Blur
>
> Recover Browser
>
> Reset Integrity
>
> Display:
>
> Current Integrity
>
> Current Active Violations
>
> Current Timeline
>
> Current Event Count
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Configuration
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Move all monitoring thresholds into configuration.
>
> Examples:
>
> Grace period
>
> Recovery timeout
>
> Warning escalation timing
>
> Penalty values
>
> Maximum warnings
>
> Integrity deductions
>
> No hardcoded values.
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Performance
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Ensure:
>
> No duplicate events
>
> No duplicate detector instances
>
> No unnecessary React renders
>
> Proper cleanup
>
> Memory leak prevention
>
> Timeline updates efficiently
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------
> Validation
> ------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Verify:
>
> ✓ DetectorManager lifecycle.
>
> ✓ Monitoring starts automatically after verification.
>
> ✓ Monitoring stops after exam completion.
>
> ✓ Active violations update instead of duplicating.
>
> ✓ Recovery closes the same event.
>
> ✓ Duration tracking works correctly.
>
> ✓ Timeline updates live.
>
> ✓ Integrity Engine responds to active violations.
>
> ✓ Warning escalation works.
>
> ✓ Development monitor works.
>
> ✓ Production build passes.
>
> ✓ Development tools are excluded from production.
>
> ✓ git diff --check passes.
>
> Do NOT implement any new AI models or detectors in this sprint.
>
> This sprint focuses entirely on converting the existing browser and vision systems into a reusable continuous integrity monitoring framework with lifecycle-based events, live timelines, configurable integrity scoring, and future-ready detector management.

Implemented Sprint P5 without commits, tags, or pushes.

### Main changes

- Added local Silero VAD inference using ONNX Runtime Web.
- Replaced production amplitude-only speech detection with model probabilities.
- Added persistent exam-object detection.
- Calibrated phone detection with smoothing, area, persistence, and lost-frame handling.
- Extended `DetectorEvidence` with confidence, stability, duration, quality, version, metadata, and timestamp.
- Added a development-only detector calibration panel.
- Preserved the shared camera, microphone, event, monitoring, and integrity architecture.

### Key files

Added:

- `src/exam/services/SileroVadRuntime.js`

- `package-lock.json`

### Silero VAD decision

Silero VAD V5 was selected because it:

- Runs entirely inside the browser.
- Provides actual speech probabilities.
- Requires no cloud API or audio upload.
- Has a browser-compatible ONNX model.
- Can consume PCM from the existing `AudioService`.

The high-level VAD package microphone controller was deliberately not used because it would create another audio pipeline. The packaged Silero model is instead executed directly through ONNX Runtime Web using the existing microphone stream and `AudioContext`.

Amplitude is now only a secondary feature for estimating non-speech noise confidence. It no longer determines speech.

### Object detection decision

The existing MediaPipe EfficientDet Lite0 pipeline remains in use because it:

- Already participates in the shared inference scheduler.
- Avoids another model and camera loop.
- Reliably exposes COCO `cell phone` and `book` categories.
- Has substantially lower complexity than introducing another YOLO runtime.

The current model does not reliably distinguish tablets, notebooks, printed papers, or calculators. These capabilities are explicitly reported as unsupported rather than producing misleading classifications. Supporting them properly will require trained custom weights in a future model upgrade.

### Phone calibration

Phone detection now supports configurable:

- Minimum confidence
- Minimum visible area
- Minimum persistence
- Maximum lost frames
- Camera-distance compensation
- Confidence smoothing
- Detection window
- Recovery persistence
- Detector version

Brief appearances do not create violations, and short detection losses retain the existing event instead of producing flicker or duplicate deductions.

### Performance impact

- Silero model: approximately 2.33 MB.
- ONNX WASM runtime: approximately 13.48 MB, loaded only with the VAD runtime.
- VAD runtime JavaScript chunk: approximately 73 KB.
- One microphone stream and one `AudioContext`.
- One camera scheduler and existing MediaPipe object inference.
- No additional camera loop.
- No microphone or camera data leaves the browser.

### Validation

Passed:

- `npm run validate:exam`
- `npm run validate:vision`
- `npm run validate:monitoring`
- `npm run validate:ai-detectors`
- `npm run validate:secure-exam`
- `npm run build`
- `git diff --check`

The development calibration panel was confirmed absent from the production bundle.

### Known limitations

- Silero provides speech probability, not semantic audio classification. It cannot definitively label music, keyboards, fans, barking, or whispers.
- Persistence and noise-confidence thresholds reduce transient keyboard/fan alerts, but acoustic testing across real devices is still required.
- Whisper sensitivity depends heavily on microphone gain and noise suppression.
- EfficientDet cannot reliably cover every requested exam object without custom training.
- Phone calibration needs real-device testing across camera distances, orientations, lighting conditions, and partial occlusion.
- Existing Pyodide and bundle-size build warnings remain unchanged.

### Before Sprint P6

Recommended next steps:

- Run a structured detector calibration study across representative devices.
- Establish labeled audio and camera test fixtures.
- Record detector version and configuration snapshots in integrity reports.
- Define evidence-retention and privacy policies.
- Establish certificate issuance thresholds using both exam score and integrity report outcomes.

### Architecture changes

- Added explicit audio pipeline states:
  - `UNINITIALIZED`
  - `REQUESTING_PERMISSION`
  - `PERMISSION_DENIED`
  - `INITIALIZING_AUDIO_CONTEXT`
  - `INITIALIZING_VAD`
  - `READY`
  - `FAILED`
  - `RECOVERING`
- Added [AudioDiagnostics](/C:/Work/MiTutoraPro/src/exam/models/AudioDiagnostics.js).
- Hardened [AudioService](/C:/Work/MiTutoraPro/src/exam/services/AudioService.js).

- Added configurable retry, timeout, health-check, buffer, and model-integrity settings.
- Added focused automated validation in `scripts/validate-audio-stability.mjs`.

### Browser compatibility

Supports standard `AudioContext` and `webkitAudioContext`, optional Permissions API, and graceful errors for:

- Unsupported browsers
- Missing MediaDevices
- Permission denial
- Missing microphones
- Suspended AudioContext
- Closed AudioContext
- Device disconnection

Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Firefox-compatible browser APIs are used.

### Recovery behavior

- Suspended contexts automatically call `resume()`.
- Foreground tab restoration checks audio health.
- Closed contexts recreate the audio pipeline.
- `devicechange` triggers clean microphone reacquisition.
- Microphone and model initialization use configurable exponential backoff.
- Simultaneous recovery signals share one promise, preventing duplicate streams and contexts.
- Stale or failed VAD inference triggers model recovery.
- Permission denial and unsupported-browser errors are not repeatedly retried.

### Silero hardening

Added validation for:

- ONNX Runtime availability
- Model download response
- SHA-256 model checksum
- Model session initialization
- Input tensor shape
- State output shape
- Probability output shape
- Finite inference probability
- Inference latency
- Stale inference heartbeat

### Architecture changes

### Acoustic event types

- Silence
- Candidate speaking

- Continuous conversation
- Music estimated
- Media playback estimated
- Keyboard typing estimated

- Saturated/clipping microphone
- Muted microphone
- Disconnected microphone
- Unknown audio

Speaker attribution, music, media, and typing are explicitly estimates rather than definitive classifications.

### Configuration additions

All new behavior is configurable, including:

- Speech persistence
- Conversation duration and recovery timeout
- Remote-speaker confidence
- Music and media confidence
- Media persistence
- Typing confidence and transient patterns

- Loud-noise multiplier

Fixed the fetch binding issue in `VadInferenceService.js`.

Root cause:
- `globalThis.fetch` was stored as a detached function.
- Calling it through `this.fetcher()` supplied the service instance as its receiver instead of `Window`.
- Firefox rejected this with: `'fetch' called on an object that does not implement interface Window`.

The native fetch is now invoked through a wrapper:

```js
(...args) => globalThis.fetch(...args)
```

Explicitly injecting `window.fetch` is also handled safely.

# P6 Planning Audit

## Executive Summary

The existing certification/proctoring foundation is structurally sound for an in-browser runtime, but it is not yet a secure or persistent certification workflow.

The current implementation:

- Holds the exam session, answers, timer, monitoring data, and result entirely in memory.
- Ships correct answers to the browser.
- Calculates exam and integrity scores in client code.
- Has no reload recovery, server deadline, heartbeat, persistent attempt, or exactly-once submission.
- Allows course progress and certificates to be written through user-owned Firestore repositories.
- Seeds mock earned certificates into Firestore for new users.
- Contains no Firestore rules or emulator configuration in the repository, so deployed enforcement cannot be verified.

P6 should introduce a persistent `ExamAttempt` aggregate and a narrow trusted backend boundary for attempt creation, state transitions, scoring, certification decisions, and certificate issuance.

Client-side detectors should remain responsible for observation. They must not become authoritative.

Recommended outcome states:

- `CERTIFIED`
- `NOT_CERTIFIED`
- `REVIEW_REQUIRED`
- `INCOMPLETE`

`FAILED` should not be used as the certification outcome because it conflates assessment failure, integrity failure, technical failure, and abandoned attempts.

No files were changed during this audit.

---

## Current Architecture

### Current dependency graph

```text
App
└── ExamExperience
    └── ExamProvider
        ├── ExamSession
        │   └── runtime state and timestamps
        │
        ├── React state
        │   ├── answers
        │   ├── current question
        │   └── generated result
        │
        ├── VisionManager
        │   ├── CameraService
        │   ├── VisionInferenceService
        │   ├── AudioService
        │   ├── VadInferenceService
        │   └── vision/audio detectors
        │
        ├── MonitoringSession
        │   ├── DetectorManager
        │   ├── BrowserMonitor
        │   ├── EventLifecycleManager
        │   └── MonitoringTimeline
        │
        ├── EventBus
        │   └── IntegrityEngine
        │       └── WarningManager
        │
        └── UI
            ├── EnvironmentCheckPage
            ├── ExamPage
            └── ExamResultPage
```

The central orchestration point is [ExamProvider.jsx](./src/exam/context/ExamProvider.jsx:17). It constructs all runtime engines and also owns answers, navigation, submission, scoring, cancellation, and result generation.

### Current exam state machine

[ExamSession.js](./src/exam/engine/ExamSession.js:1) supports:

```text
IDLE
→ ENVIRONMENT_CHECK
→ READY
→ RUNNING
→ COMPLETED
→ IDLE
```

This is suitable as a local runtime controller but is too coarse for persistent certification attempts. In particular, `COMPLETED` currently includes successful submission and cancellation.

### Current submission flow

[ExamProvider.jsx](./src/exam/context/ExamProvider.jsx:141) performs submission synchronously:

1. Checks that the in-memory session is `RUNNING`.
2. Stops monitoring.
3. Transitions to `COMPLETED`.
4. Compares answers against `correctOptionId`.
5. Creates the integrity report.
6. Stores the result in React state.

There is no asynchronous persistence, transaction, submission identifier, or recovery path.

The local state guard prevents most duplicate clicks in one JavaScript instance, but it cannot prevent duplication across refreshes, tabs, devices, or network retries.

### Current timer

[ExamPage.jsx](./src/exam/pages/ExamPage.jsx:20) calculates time from:

```text
session.duration - (Date.now() - session.startTime)
```

The timer is client-authoritative. Reloading destroys `startTime`, and modifying the system clock can affect the result.

### Current exam content

[sampleExam.json](./src/exam/data/sampleExam.json:1) is bundled into the frontend and contains every `correctOptionId`. A candidate can inspect the bundle or alter the scoring code.

---

## Current Data Flow

### Environment verification

```text
Camera/audio/browser APIs
        ↓
VisionManager
        ↓
DetectorStatus objects
        ↓
Readiness score and stability duration
        ↓
VisionResult.VERIFIED
        ↓
ExamSession.READY
```

The standalone setup test and the actual exam each create separate runtime managers. A previous standalone setup result is not reused when starting the exam.

### Continuous monitoring

```text
Detector output
      ↓
EventBus
      ↓
MonitoringSession
      ↓
EventLifecycleManager
      ↓
IntegrityEvent
      ↓
IntegrityEngine
      ↓
WarningManager + IntegrityReport
```

Lifecycle events are correctly deduplicated by violation type. Recovery updates the same event rather than creating a second violation.

### Result generation

```text
Answers + browser-bundled answer key
                ↓
          Client exam score

Monitoring timeline + client configuration
                ↓
        Client integrity score

Exam score displayed directly in UI
```

There is no separate `CertificationEngine` yet.

---

## Runtime vs Persistent State

| Data | Current owner | Current state | Persist in P6? | Recommendation |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Exam attempt | `ExamProvider` | Runtime only | Yes | Persistent authoritative aggregate |
| Exam definition | `sampleExam.json` | Bundled | Yes | Versioned definition; never expose answer key |
| Questions | `sampleExam.json` | Bundled | Yes | Persist/version sanitized candidate payload |
| Correct answers | Browser bundle | Client-visible | Yes, trusted side only | Never return to candidate |
| Selected answers | React state | Runtime only | Yes | Autosave for recovery |
| Current question | React state | Runtime only | Optional | Persist as resume convenience, not authority |
| Timer remaining | `ExamPage` | Derived client-side | No | Persist `startedAt` and `expiresAt`, derive remaining |
| Start/end timestamps | `ExamSession` | Runtime client time | Yes | Server timestamps |
| Submission state | `ExamSession` | Runtime only | Yes | Transactional attempt state |
| Exam score | `ExamProvider` | Client-calculated | Yes | Trusted evaluation result |
| Environment result | `VisionManager` | Runtime only | Yes | Persist final structured summary |
| Readiness score | `VisionManager` | Runtime only | Yes | Persist final score and rule version |
| Live detector status | Detectors | Runtime | No | Ephemeral operational state |
| Integrity score | `IntegrityEngine` | Runtime client state | Yes | Trusted recomputation from submitted events |
| Warnings | `WarningManager` | Runtime only | Yes | Final warning ledger |
| Active violations | Lifecycle manager | Runtime | Partially | Persist normalized lifecycle events, not hot UI state |
| Integrity timeline | Monitoring session | Runtime | Yes | Structured event documents |
| Monitoring duration | Monitoring session | Runtime | Yes | Persist aggregate timestamps/duration |
| Detector evidence | Detector statuses | Runtime | Selectively | Structured measurements only |
| Camera frames | Browser/media pipeline | Transient | No | Never persist |
| Audio samples | Audio/VAD buffers | Transient | No | Never persist |
| Biometric images | Not created | Not retained | No | Explicitly prohibit |
| Model tensors | Inference services | Transient | No | Dispose and never serialize |
| Certification decision | Does not exist | — | Yes | Trusted, immutable final result |
| Course completion | Progress document | Firestore | Already persisted | Reference existing state; do not duplicate |
| User identity | Firebase Auth/User document | Persisted | Already persisted | Reference UID |

### Media retention finding

No `MediaRecorder`, recording upload, image capture, or audio persistence exists.

Transient processing includes:

- Camera stream attached to a `<video>`.
- A 64×36 luminance frame used for brightness/motion.
- Face landmarks and object detections held in memory.
- Short audio buffers and ONNX tensors.
- Structured evidence such as confidence, duration, labels, pose values, and bounding boxes.

P6 should persist only normalized structured evidence. It should explicitly reject blobs, base64 images, audio arrays, tensors, and media URLs.

---

## Proposed Firestore Model

### Recommended minimum model

```text
certificationExams/{examId}

users/{uid}/certifications/{courseId}

examAttempts/{attemptId}
examAttempts/{attemptId}/responses/current
examAttempts/{attemptId}/integrityEvents/{eventId}

certificates/{credentialId}
```

A separate `examSessions`, `examSlots`, or `integrityReports` top-level collection is not necessary for P6.

### 1. `certificationExams/{examId}`

Purpose: immutable, versioned certification definition metadata.

Important fields:

```js
{
  id,
  courseId,
  title,
  version,
  durationMs,
  passingScore,
  integrityPolicyId,
  questionSetVersion,
  questionCount,
  published,
  effectiveFrom,
  createdAt,
  updatedAt
}
```

The candidate-facing question payload must not contain answer keys. Answer keys and evaluation rules must be accessible only to trusted code.

Immutable once an attempt references it:

- `version`
- `questionSetVersion`
- `durationMs`
- `passingScore`
- integrity policy reference

A new exam version should create a new immutable version rather than mutate active attempts.

### 2. `users/{uid}/certifications/{courseId}`

Purpose: candidate-specific eligibility and summary projection.

Suggested fields:

```js
{
  courseId,
  eligibilityStatus,       // LOCKED | ELIGIBLE
  eligibleAt,
  activeAttemptId,
  latestAttemptId,
  latestDecision,
  attemptCount,
  certificateId,
  updatedAt
}
```

This document provides a canonical location for:

- Duplicate-active-attempt prevention.
- Course certification availability.
- Certificates-page summaries.
- Fast resume lookup.

`activeAttemptId` must be changed transactionally with attempt creation/finalization.

### 3. `examAttempts/{attemptId}`

Purpose: authoritative lifecycle aggregate.

Suggested fields:

```js
{
  id,
  ownerUid,
  courseId,
  examId,
  examVersion,

  state,
  scheduledFor,
  createdAt,
  verificationStartedAt,
  verifiedAt,
  startedAt,
  expiresAt,
  submittedAt,
  finalizedAt,

  sessionId,
  lastHeartbeatAt,
  heartbeatSequence,
  recoveryDeadline,

  environmentSummary,
  submissionId,
  submissionReason,

  examResult,
  integrityResult,
  certificationDecision,

  configVersions,
  schemaVersion,
  updatedAt
}
```

Mutable during the attempt:

- Lifecycle state
- Scheduling fields
- heartbeat/session lease
- environment summary
- submission metadata

Immutable after submission:

- Identity and exam version
- start/deadline timestamps
- answer snapshot/hash
- exam result
- integrity result
- certification decision

### 4. `responses/current`

Purpose: recoverable mutable answers without repeatedly rewriting the attempt aggregate.

```js
{
  answers,
  currentQuestionId,
  revision,
  updatedAt
}
```

Answers are untrusted candidate input. They become immutable when submission is accepted.

### 5. `integrityEvents/{eventId}`

Purpose: normalized event lifecycle and structured evidence.

```js
{
  id,
  type,
  status,
  startedAt,
  endedAt,
  durationMs,
  severity,
  warningLevel,
  deductions,
  evidence,
  detectorId,
  detectorVersion,
  modelVersion,
  ruleSetVersion,
  createdAt,
  updatedAt
}
```

Evidence must be allow-listed. No arbitrary metadata blob should be accepted.

### 6. `certificates/{credentialId}`

Purpose: authoritative public credential record.

```js
{
  credentialId,
  ownerUid,
  courseId,
  examAttemptId,
  examVersion,
  issuedAt,
  status,             // ACTIVE | REVOKED
  verificationCode,
  certificateVersion
}
```

Certificate creation, status changes, and revocation must be server-only.

A verification endpoint should expose only public credential details rather than the full document or owner UID.

### Why not separate collections?

- `examSlots`: defer until capacity-based scheduling exists. `scheduledFor` is sufficient for P6.
- `examSessions`: session/lease fields belong to the attempt aggregate.
- `integrityReports`: the final summary can be embedded in the attempt; detailed events remain a subcollection.
- `certifications`: use the existing user-scoped certification projection plus authoritative `certificates`.

---

## Exam Attempt State Machine

### Persisted states

```text
CREATED
→ SCHEDULED
→ VERIFYING
→ READY
→ RUNNING
→ SUBMITTED
→ EVALUATING
→ FINALIZED
```

Terminal exceptional states:

```text
CANCELLED
EXPIRED
ABANDONED
```

`SUBMITTING` should be a local UI state, not a durable domain state. The server should atomically move `RUNNING → SUBMITTED`.

### Transition table

| From | To | Trigger | Atomic? | Reversible? |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| — | CREATED | Trusted create-attempt operation | Yes | No |
| CREATED | SCHEDULED | Candidate books allowed time | Yes | Until verification |
| SCHEDULED | VERIFYING | Candidate begins setup | Yes | Resume allowed |
| VERIFYING | READY | Verified environment summary accepted | Yes | May expire |
| READY | RUNNING | Trusted start operation | Yes | No |
| RUNNING | SUBMITTED | Manual or timeout submission | Yes | No |
| SUBMITTED | EVALUATING | Evaluation worker claims attempt | Yes | No |
| EVALUATING | FINALIZED | Decision and optional certificate written | Yes | No |
| CREATED/SCHEDULED | CANCELLED | Candidate cancellation | Yes | No |
| SCHEDULED/READY | EXPIRED | Start window expires | Yes | No |
| RUNNING | ABANDONED | Recovery window and deadline expire | Yes | No |

Invalid transitions must be rejected centrally, including:

- `READY → FINALIZED`
- `RUNNING → READY`
- `SUBMITTED → RUNNING`
- Any terminal state back to an active state
- Changing exam version after creation

### Certification decision model

Keep lifecycle separate from outcome:

```js
PENDING
CERTIFIED
NOT_CERTIFIED
REVIEW_REQUIRED
INCOMPLETE
```

Examples:

- Passing score and acceptable integrity: `CERTIFIED`
- Exam score below threshold: `NOT_CERTIFIED`
- Integrity threshold or ambiguous evidence: `REVIEW_REQUIRED`
- Cancelled, expired, or abandoned: `INCOMPLETE`

---

## Recovery Strategy

### Current behavior

| Failure | Current result |
|---|---|
| Refresh/tab close/browser crash | Entire attempt lost |
| Network loss | Exam continues locally; nothing syncs |
| Camera disconnect | Recovery attempted |
| Microphone disconnect | Recovery attempted |
| Fullscreen exit | Lifecycle violation |
| Laptop sleep | Client timer pauses operationally but wall-clock calculation jumps on wake |
| Return after several minutes | No authoritative recovery decision |
| Second tab/device | Independent duplicate attempt possible |

### Recommended recovery design

1. Attempt start writes server-owned `startedAt` and `expiresAt`.
2. Client derives remaining time from `expiresAt`; never persist remaining seconds.
3. Server returns a clock offset derived from server time.
4. A unique `sessionId` or lease is assigned when the attempt starts.
5. Heartbeats include a monotonically increasing sequence.
6. `users/{uid}/certifications/{courseId}.activeAttemptId` prevents parallel attempts.
7. Reload queries the active attempt and reacquires its session lease transactionally.
8. Recovery never modifies `startedAt` or `expiresAt`.
9. Recovery is allowed only inside a configurable recovery window.
10. A scheduled trusted worker finalizes expired attempts even if the browser never returns.

Offline behavior should be bounded:

- Answers and integrity events may remain temporarily queued in memory.
- Previously acknowledged server state must never be overwritten by stale cache.
- The UI must visibly indicate unsynchronized state.
- Starting an exam should require connectivity.
- Final certification cannot be produced offline.

---

## Exactly-Once Submission Strategy

### Client protection

Use a stable per-attempt `submissionId` and an in-memory promise lock:

```text
manual submit ┐
              ├→ submitAttempt(attemptId, submissionId)
timeout submit┘
```

Both manual and timeout paths must call the same service method.

### Trusted transaction

The submission operation should:

1. Read the attempt.
2. Verify ownership/session.
3. If the same `submissionId` is already accepted, return the existing result.
4. If the attempt is already submitted under another request, return its immutable submission status.
5. Reject invalid lifecycle states.
6. Validate the authoritative deadline.
7. Freeze the current response revision.
8. Write `SUBMITTED`, `submittedAt`, `submissionReason`, and `submissionId`.
9. Clear `activeAttemptId` only during finalization or terminal handling.

Evaluation should claim the attempt transactionally:

```text
SUBMITTED → EVALUATING
```

Finalization should atomically write:

- Exam result
- Integrity result
- Certification decision
- Certificate when applicable
- Certification projection update
- `FINALIZED`

Retries must return the existing decision rather than issue another certificate.

---

## Certification Decision Architecture

Recommended target:

```text
Exam responses
      ↓
Trusted ExamScoringEngine
      ↓
ExamResult

Structured integrity events
      ↓
Trusted IntegrityEvaluationEngine
      ↓
IntegrityResult

ExamResult + IntegrityResult + Eligibility
      ↓
Trusted CertificationEngine
      ↓
CertificationDecision
      ↓
CertificateIssuer
```

The new `CertificationEngine` should not live inside React, `ExamProvider`, `IntegrityEngine`, or `CertificatesPage`.

It should be a deterministic domain engine executed from trusted server-side code. Client code may share decision enums and DTO validation, but must not execute the authoritative decision.

---

## Integrity Report Persistence

The current [IntegrityReport.js](./src/exam/models/IntegrityReport.js:1) contains only:

- Score
- Warning count
- Timeline
- Generated timestamp

P6 should add:

- Attempt ID
- Monitoring start/end/duration
- Initial and final integrity scores
- Warning ledger
- Deduction ledger with rule IDs
- Normalized lifecycle events
- Detector and model versions
- Integrity rule-set version
- Configuration hash
- Environment verification reference
- Final review flags
- Report schema version

Persist:

- Event type and lifecycle
- Confidence/stability/duration
- Structured measurements
- Detector/model/rule versions
- Applied deductions and escalation levels

Do not persist:

- Camera frames
- Face images
- Audio recordings
- Raw PCM samples
- Raw landmarks when not required
- Model tensors
- Canvas pixel buffers
- Media streams
- Arbitrary diagnostic objects

Configuration version and hash are necessary because current penalty behavior comes from [ExamConfig.js](./src/exam/engine/ExamConfig.js:4). Historical decisions must remain reproducible after configuration changes.

---

## Course Completion Integration

### Current representation

[LearningProgressContext.jsx](./src/progress/LearningProgressContext.jsx:24) derives completion from the longest consecutive completed lesson prefix.

Persisted progress contains:

- Completed/visited lessons
- Completed modules
- Sequential completion count
- Course percentage
- Quiz and exercise state

### Current trust level

Course completion is not trustworthy enough for secure credential issuance because:

- Completion is calculated in the browser.
- The browser writes its own progress.
- Development includes `markAllLessonsComplete`.
- No repository Firestore rules are available for verification.
- A user can potentially alter their progress document outside the UI.

P6 should not duplicate all lesson progress into certification records.

Recommended integration:

```text
Existing progress document
        ↓
Trusted eligibility evaluator
        ↓
users/{uid}/certifications/{courseId}
        eligibilityStatus = ELIGIBLE
```

Until learning completion becomes server-verifiable, eligibility is suitable for product gating but not strong certification security. This limitation should be documented explicitly.

---

## Security / Trust Boundary

### Client-observed but untrusted

- Camera availability
- Face/object detections
- Audio/VAD classifications
- Browser visibility/fullscreen state
- Answers
- Detector evidence
- Integrity event emission
- Environment readiness
- Heartbeat requests

These signals are useful, but a modified client can omit or fabricate them.

### Trusted operations required

- Attempt creation and uniqueness
- Server timestamps and deadline
- State transitions
- Answer-key access
- Exam scoring
- Integrity policy application
- Certification decision
- Certificate issuance/revocation
- Final result immutability
- Attempt expiration
- Credential verification response

### Firestore assessment

Firebase SDK access is correctly isolated to Firebase/repository infrastructure. Components do not directly import Firestore.

However:

- [BaseRepository.js](./src/repositories/firestore/BaseRepository.js:61) provides ordinary client `set`, `update`, and batch writes.
- It has no transaction or server timestamp support.
- User certificates currently use the same user-owned persistence pattern.
- No `firestore.rules`, indexes, or emulator configuration exists in the repository.
- Therefore, deployed data protection cannot be established from source control.

A secure P6 requires callable HTTPS/Cloud Functions or an equivalent trusted API. Firestore rules alone cannot safely recompute exam scores or certification decisions.

---

## Technical Debt & Risks

### Critical

1. **Client-visible answer keys and client scoring**
   Correct options are bundled in `sampleExam.json`.

2. **Client-authoritative integrity and certification inputs**
   Detector events can be suppressed or fabricated in a modified client.

3. **Mock earned certificates are persisted as real user data**
   [CertificateService.js](./src/certificates/CertificateService.js:10) seeds `mockCertificates` when Firestore is empty.

4. **No verifiable Firestore security rules in the repository**
   Final-result immutability cannot currently be proven.

5. **No persistent attempt identity**
   Refresh or a second tab can create a logically separate attempt.

### High

1. No exactly-once network submission.
2. Client-only timestamps and timer.
3. Course completion is user-writable.
4. `COMPLETED` conflates submission and cancellation.
5. `markEnvironmentReady` is publicly exposed by the context.
6. Integrity reports omit configuration and detector versions.
7. Detector stop methods may be asynchronous, but `DetectorManager.stop()` does not await them.
8. Monitoring enters `RUNNING` before all detectors successfully start.
9. StrictMode/start-stop lifecycle races remain possible for asynchronous detectors.
10. Existing `UserDataService` offline cache semantics are inappropriate for authoritative exam state.

### Medium

1. Timer interval is recreated whenever `submitExam` changes with answer state.
2. Standalone setup verification is disconnected from the exam attempt.
3. `EventBus.emit()` does not isolate listener exceptions.
4. Event IDs use process-local counters and timestamps; they are not reload-safe.
5. Evidence objects are class instances and need explicit Firestore DTO serialization.
6. Integrity timeline and warning state have overlapping representations.
7. Browser and vision monitoring share a `VisionManager` lifecycle through nested managers.
8. Base repositories read documents immediately after writes, increasing cost.

### Low

1. No dedicated question/result models.
2. Version constants are spread across detector configuration.
3. Existing documentation still describes certificates as a replaceable user repository rather than an authoritative credential system.

---

## P6 Scope

### Must have

- Persistent attempt aggregate
- Versioned exam definition
- Candidate-safe question payload
- Trusted answer-key access and scoring
- Server timestamps and deadline
- Transactional state transitions
- Single active attempt enforcement
- Answer autosave and reload recovery
- Heartbeat/session lease
- Exactly-once submission
- Timeout finalization
- Structured integrity event persistence
- Trusted certification decision
- Immutable certificate issuance
- Firestore rules and emulator tests
- Removal of mock certificate issuance behavior

### Should have

- Basic booking with `scheduledFor`
- Recovery-window UI
- Unsynchronized/offline indicator
- Review-required workflow state
- Attempt history
- Config/model version audit fields
- Feature flag for staged rollout

### Defer to P7

- Human review dashboard
- Administrative override workflow
- Certificate revocation UI
- Capacity-aware scheduling
- Email notifications
- Rich attempt analytics
- Long-term retention automation

### Defer to V2

- Face recognition
- Liveness detection
- Screen recording
- OCR
- External monitor detection
- Advanced audio accuracy
- Additional AI detectors
- Multi-camera or device attestation
- High-assurance identity verification

## Migration / Backward Compatibility

1. Keep existing learning progress documents unchanged.
2. Introduce schema-versioned certification documents alongside existing data.
3. Do not treat existing mock certificate records as authoritative.
4. Mark legacy certificates as demo/legacy or ignore them in the new service.
5. Do not automatically issue certificates from current client-written progress.
6. Backfill only eligibility projections where policy permits.
7. Release behind a feature flag.
8. Run both certificate readers temporarily, clearly separating verified credentials from legacy demonstrations.
9. Stop mock seeding before enabling authoritative issuance.
10. Migrate `sampleExam.json` to server-controlled exam content before enabling real certification.

No existing exam attempts require migration because none are currently persisted.

- Unauthenticated user cannot read attempt data

### Firestore rules tests

Use the Firebase Emulator Suite to test every permitted and denied operation. Current Node validation scripts are useful for engine behavior but are insufficient for persistence concurrency and security.

## Implementation Order

1. Define attempt, result, integrity, decision, and eligibility contracts.
2. Add Firestore rules and emulator tests before UI integration.
3. Add trusted attempt creation/start/heartbeat operations.
4. Add sanitized exam delivery and trusted scoring.
5. Add response autosave and reload recovery.
6. Add integrity event serialization and persistence.
7. Add idempotent submission and timeout finalization.
8. Implement trusted certification decision and issuance.
9. Integrate `ExamProvider` with the service boundary.
10. Replace mock certificate seeding.
11. Add Certificates-page eligibility and attempt states.
12. Perform staged migration and remove production sample/mock data.
13. Run lifecycle, concurrency, security, and recovery suites.

---

## Risks

- Client detector events remain intrinsically untrusted even after persistence.
- Existing course progress is not authoritative enough for high-stakes eligibility.
- Firestore document size requires events to remain a subcollection.
- Frequent heartbeats and event updates can create cost and write hot spots.
- Offline recovery can accidentally overwrite newer state unless revisions are enforced.
- Moving scoring server-side requires separating question content from answer keys.
- Legacy mock certificates can be mistaken for real credentials if not explicitly isolated.
- A client-only P6 would provide persistence but not defensible certification security.

---

## Final Recommendation

Implement P6 as a persistent certification lifecycle with a narrow trusted backend boundary.

Keep the existing Exam Engine, MonitoringSession, VisionManager, detectors, and EventBus as runtime infrastructure. Add an authoritative `ExamAttempt` aggregate around them. Persist only structured evidence and lifecycle state. Move scoring, final integrity evaluation, certification decisions, deadlines, idempotency, and certificate issuance to trusted code.

Do not use the generic user-owned `UserDataService` write path for authoritative attempts, results, or certificates.

The minimum secure V1 requires trusted server-side operations. Without them, the platform can offer a practice assessment with monitoring signals, but it cannot safely claim that exam scores, integrity results, or certificates are authoritative.

Implemented Sprint P7 without committing, tagging, or pushing.

## P7 implementation summary

- Replaced eligibility based on client-writable progress with a server-owned trusted completion ledger.
- Added manifest-driven course completion evaluation without hardcoded lesson/module counts.
- Added immutable integrity reports with aggregated violations and version snapshots.
- Added candidate-safe certification decision explanations.
- Added durable, trusted `REVIEW_REQUIRED` workflow.
- Added privileged review resolution using Firebase custom claims.
- Added immutable, idempotent certification audit events.
- Refined candidate results to avoid exposing raw detector details or anti-cheating thresholds.
- Preserved existing P1–P6 exam, monitoring, vision, audio, recovery, and submission architecture.

## Trusted eligibility

New flow:

```text
Lesson completion
→ Trusted callable Function
→ Published course manifest validation
→ Server-owned trustedCourseProgress ledger
→ CourseCompletionEngine
→ Certification eligibility projection
```

Firestore:

```text
users/{uid}/trustedCourseProgress/{courseId}
users/{uid}/certifications/{courseId}
```

Changing the legacy `users/{uid}/progress/{courseId}` document no longer unlocks certification.

Eligibility now includes:

- Status
- Course content version
- Completion percentage
- Required lesson count
- Completed required lesson count
- Evaluation timestamp
- Eligibility policy version

## Integrity reports

Finalization creates:

```text
integrityReports/{reportId}
```

Reports contain:

- Integrity score and status
- Aggregated violation categories
- Occurrence counts
- Total and maximum durations
- Monitoring duration
- Timeline summary
- Detector and model versions
- Exam and policy versions
- Content hash
- Schema version

No raw audio, images, video, frames, tensors, or biometric data are stored.

## Certification decisions

Trusted decisions remain:

- `CERTIFIED`
- `NOT_CERTIFIED`
- `REVIEW_REQUIRED`
- `INCOMPLETE`

Each decision now includes a candidate-safe explanation without exposing sensitive thresholds or confidence values.

## Review workflow

Created:

```text
certificationReviews/{reviewId}
```

Lifecycle:

```text
PENDING → IN_REVIEW → RESOLVED
```

Resolution:

```text
CERTIFIED | NOT_CERTIFIED
```

Review operations require server-managed Firebase custom claims:

- `admin: true`
- `certificationReviewer: true`

Candidate-controlled profile fields cannot grant reviewer access.

Review-required attempts remain finalized but receive no certificate until a trusted certified resolution.

## Audit trail

Created immutable events under:

```text
examAttempts/{attemptId}/auditEvents/{eventId}
```

Covered events include:

- Attempt creation/start/recovery
- Submission
- Evaluation start/completion
- Decision creation
- Review creation/resolution
- Certificate issuance

Event IDs are deterministic where appropriate, preventing duplicate audit records during retries.

## Security changes

Candidates cannot directly:

- Write trusted completion records
- Modify eligibility
- Modify integrity reports
- Create or resolve reviews
- Modify audit events
- Modify final scores or decisions
- Issue or modify certificates
- Read finalized raw integrity events

Candidates can read their own:

- Certification projection
- Final attempt result
- Integrity summary
- Review status
- Certificate
- Audit trail

## Read-only diagnosis

No source files, Firebase resources, rules, or configuration were changed.

### Root cause

`recordTrustedLessonCompletion` does not exist at the production endpoint being called.

Verified directly:

```text
OPTIONS https://us-central1-mi-tutora-pro.cloudfunctions.net/recordTrustedLessonCompletion
Status: 404 Not Found
```

The Firebase CLI also reported that the Cloud Functions API is disabled or has never been enabled for `mi-tutora-pro`. Consequently, the CLI could not find a deployed Functions inventory.

The browser reports this as CORS because the nonexistent endpoint’s 404 response has no callable-function CORS headers. It is an endpoint/deployment failure, not a CORS-policy failure.

Additionally, the entire `functions/` directory and P7 frontend integration are currently untracked in Git. This strongly indicates the P7 function exists only in the local working tree and was never included in a production deployment.

### Function contract

- Exact export: `recordTrustedLessonCompletion`
- Backend type: Firebase Functions v2 `onCall`
- Configured region: implicit default `us-central1`
- Frontend invocation: Firebase `httpsCallable()`
- Requested endpoint: correct for that name and default region

Relevant code:

- [functions/src/index.js](./functions/src/index.js:41)
- [src/firebase/functions.js](./src/firebase/functions.js:4)
- [TrustedCompletionService.js](./src/progress/TrustedCompletionService.js:5)

There are no export-name collisions or alternate names.

### Project verification

The frontend environment uses:

```text
VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=mi-tutora-pro
VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=mi-tutora-pro.firebaseapp.com
```

The CLI was explicitly queried with `--project mi-tutora-pro`, so the frontend and inspected deployment target match.

There is no `.firebaserc`; deployments should therefore continue using an explicit `--project mi-tutora-pro` argument unless one is added later.

### Authentication and validation

The callable security design is correct:

- `httpsCallable()` automatically sends the current Firebase Auth token.
- The server requires `request.auth.uid`.
- The authoritative UID comes from the verified callable context.
- The client does not supply a UID.
- The service checks that course metadata exists and is published.
- It downloads the version selected by Firestore metadata.
- It verifies that the lesson exists in the published manifest.
- Repeating completion for the same user/course/version/lesson returns the existing record without another Firestore write.

One unrelated hardening opportunity remains: the downloaded manifest’s `id` and internal version are not explicitly compared with the requested course ID and Firestore metadata version. This does not cause the current 404.

### Required source changes

None are required to fix this endpoint failure. The source already uses the correct callable architecture and matching function name.

Optional hardening would affect:

- [CourseCompletionService.js](./functions/src/certification/CourseCompletionService.js:14) — explicitly compare manifest identity/version with Firestore metadata.
- `.firebaserc` — optionally pin the default project to prevent accidental deployments elsewhere.

Neither should be treated as the current production fix.

### Required production action

First enable the Cloud Functions API for `mi-tutora-pro`. Then deploy the callable:

```powershell
npx.cmd firebase-tools deploy --only functions:recordTrustedLessonCompletion --project mi-tutora-pro
```

Because this is a v2 callable, Firebase should manage callable CORS handling automatically. Do not add wildcard CORS headers.

After deployment, verify with:

```powershell
npx.cmd firebase-tools functions:list --project mi-tutora-pro
```

The expected inventory entry is:

```text
recordTrustedLessonCompletion
Region: us-central1
Type: callable / HTTPS v2
```
